name: Delhi's AQI
description: An interactive data visualisation that exposes how clean air in Delhi has become a privilege, using personal data and narrative to shift users from awareness to discomfort.

contentBlocks.content: An interactive data visualisation that exposes how clean air in Delhi has become a privilege, using personal data and narrative to shift users from awareness to discomfort.

Clean air in Delhi has been privatized. Upper-middle-class residents buy their way out of toxic air through HEPA purifiers, sealed AC cars, and filtered offices — but the pollution doesn't disappear. It stays in the shared commons, inhabited by the people who can't afford to exit it.
This is a browser-based interactive data visualization that makes this system visible. It starts by taking inputs from users and ends with a comparative analysis.

content: Current state: Desensitised. They've normalised the crisis through capital — purifiers, AC commutes, sealed offices.
Why them: They have the social capital, economic power, and political voice to demand systemic change. They are the audience most capable of acting — and the least confronted with the need to.

contentBlocks.content: E = (C1 × t1 + C2 × t2 + ... + Cn × tn) / 24 — Time-weighted average across home, commute, and workplace over 24 hrs. Each environment has a different PM2.5 concentration.
Cigarettes/day = Daily PM2.5 (μg/m³) / 22 — Berkeley Earth equivalence formula. Translates invisible pollution into a tangible health comparison — 22 μg/m³ sustained for one day equals one cigarette.

Years Lost = ((PM2.5 - 5) / 10) × 0.98 — AQLI methodology (U. of Chicago EPIC). Every 10 μg/m³ above the WHO guideline of 5 μg/m³ reduces life expectancy by ~1 year. Applied across the residency duration.
